newsitem.title: UK: Barclays seeks Morgan's custody business.
newsitem.headline: Barclays seeks Morgan's custody business.

text.p: Britain's Barclays Plc said Monday it was in talks with Morgan Stanley & Co. about its global custody business, as banking sources confirmed the Barclays unit is up for sale.
Barclays and Morgan Stanley said only that they are "in discussions to explore the potential for future cooperation."
The move would be another step in the consolidation of the global custody business, which is becoming dominated by banks willing to make the large front-end investment required.
Custody businesses range from traditional safekeeping of securities, which in Britain is dominated by Lloyds TSB and Royal Bank of Scotland, to performance measurement and stock lending.
Barclays' custody business has 350 to 400 staff worldwide, with some working in the Far East. Securities worth about 150 billion British pounds ($239.2 billion) have been placed with the unit.

It was not clear when a deal might be finalised, but analysts said they expect Morgan Stanley to pay well under 100 million pounds ($159 million) for the business. "It could well be less than fifty million ($80 million)," said one.
